item.title: ‘Be not afraid,’ President Uchtdorf teaches at Utah Valley Institute devotional
item.description:
Speaking in Orem on Nov. 15, President Dieter F. Uchtdorf, acting president of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, drew six lessons from the Old Testament king Jehoshaphat for Utah Valley Institute of Religion listeners facing fear, worry or difficult choices. Uchtdorf warned against reading the account as a guarantee that faith makes every trial vanish, saying "Some battles are long." The complete Church News report is available at TheChurchNews.com.


Sources:

  • ‘Be not afraid,’ President Uchtdorf teaches at Utah Valley Institute devotional - deseret.com

item.title: 3 new exhibits chronicle the Salt Lake Temple’s history and influence
item.description:
Ahead of the Salt Lake Temple's first open house for the public since 1893, the downtown Church History Museum in Salt Lake City has opened three exhibits that will stay up through the Salt Lake Temple Celebration, which runs April 5 to Oct. 1, 2027. Fitly Framed Together follows the temple from construction to dedication through lesser-known contributors such as Antonio Scappatura, a Catholic stonemason from Sicily who may have cut a temple stone on display; All Nations Shall Flow Unto It gathers depictions of the temple from abroad, including a Peruvian textile and batiks from Sierra Leone and Indonesia; and One by One: Gathered unto Christ tells 55 conversion stories, among them that of Hare Teimana, a Māori chief baptized in 1882. Museum director Riley Lorimer said the hope is that visitors will be "inspired by stories that they may not have heard before" and see people of every background strengthening the church.


Sources:

  • 3 new exhibits chronicle the Salt Lake Temple’s history and influence - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Amy Ortiz

item.title: Which religion will be the world’s largest in 2035? Pew offers a projection
item.description:
A new 300-page Pew Research Center report projects that Muslims will overtake Christians as the world's largest religious group by 2035 and number about 3.6 billion to Christians' 3 billion by 2070, with lead author Conrad Hackett calling natural population increase the biggest factor, well ahead of religious switching. Pew's Alan Cooperman said the shift isn't a contest between the faiths, since most growth for each will come where it already predominates, and the report expects Congo to pass the United States as home to the most Christians by 2070, 299 million to 174 million. In the U.S., Christians are projected to slip from 62% of the population to under half by 2070 while still being the largest group, as the unaffiliated grow from 28% to 41%.


Sources:

  • Which religion will be the world’s largest in 2035? Pew offers a projection - deseret.com

item.title: Man sentenced to decades in prison for child sex abuse crimes in Ohio and Utah
item.description:
U.S. District Judge Edmund Sargus on Tuesday sentenced Wade Christofferson, 73, to 45 years in federal prison after he pleaded guilty to coercing and enticing a Utah girl under 10, to whose home he had mailed coded, sexually explicit letters from Ohio for about six months. The U.S. Attorney's Office said investigators confirmed about 20 instances of hands-on abuse of victims in Utah and Ohio, and Sargus, who said a life term wouldn't be consistent with other cases, called the sentence essentially a life sentence. U.S. Attorney Dominick S. Gerace II said the evidence showed a sexual interest in children that "spanned decades"; the defendant's older brother is President D. Todd Christofferson, second counselor in the Latter-day Saint First Presidency.


Sources:

  • Man sentenced to decades in prison for child sex abuse crimes in Ohio and Utah - deseret.com

item.title: Fear fueled Steve Young. A new bout of anxiety reveals fresh insight for following Christ
item.description:
At a BYU-Idaho devotional in Rexburg on Tuesday, former 49ers quarterback Steve Young, 65, said the separation anxiety he believed he had outgrown came back over the past year harder than anything he had felt as an adult, and that facing it showed him fear had been the deepest bargain of his life all along. Young told the 10,107 students that believing enough worry can control outcomes is "magical thinking," the same transactional mindset he has long preached against, and that Christ's repeated command not to fear invites people out of that pattern rather than asking them to be braver. He urged them to keep caring while dropping the belief that their anxiety earns God's help, saying trust "is where love leads".


Sources:

  • Fear fueled Steve Young. A new bout of anxiety reveals fresh insight for following Christ - deseret.com

item.title: Light the World turns 10 with a record number of Giving Machines
item.description:
Last year's Giving Machine donations paid for 3.5 million meals and vaccinated 500,000 children, and this season the red machines from The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, where shoppers buy goats, chickens, hygiene products and other gifts for people in need, return for a 10th year at a record 145 sites, with nine countries including South Korea, Taiwan and Hungary hosting for the first time. Speaking at Tuesday's global launch, Elder Peter M. Johnson of the Seventy called Jesus Christ "the ultimate giver and the Prince of Peace" and encouraged people to bring friends and family to a machine nearby.

  • Light the World turns 10 with a record number of Giving Machines - deseret.com

item.title: The world needs young adults now: 4 Latter-day Saint leaders’ pleas to young adults
item.description:
Four leaders of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints addressed young adults Sunday in Orem, Salt Lake City, Logan and Ogden, stressing faith in Christ, heeding prophets and serving others. Relief Society President Camille N. Johnson told the Salt Lake City group they needn't wait for school or career milestones to make a difference, saying "We need that kind of energy right now." After her devotional, Johnson joined hundreds of them making sleeping mats for homeless people; in Logan, Sister J. Anette Dennis helped assemble 3,400 humanitarian kits, while in Orem President Dieter F. Uchtdorf drew lessons from the Old Testament king Jehoshaphat and in Ogden Elder Clark G. Gilbert urged listeners to notice what a prophet repeats and pleads for.


Sources:

  • The world needs young adults now: 4 Latter-day Saint leaders’ pleas to young adults - deseret.com

item.title: How this single word can shape a life, according to Christian editor Anne Snyder
item.description:
Delivering BYU's Truman G. Madsen lecture on Tuesday, Comment magazine editor-in-chief Anne Snyder asked how the commitments people say yes to end up shaping who they become, borrowing Isaiah Berlin's contrast between foxes with many interests and hedgehogs who build around a single aim. Snyder, who identifies more with the fox, held up examples of committed lives, especially Swiss painter Manuel Dürr, picked to create a new set of 14 Stations of the Cross for St. Peter's Basilica, who came to accept that the meaning of his work was not his to determine. She closed by wishing students a commitment "substantial enough to shape a life but alive enough to keep listening."


Sources:

  • How this single word can shape a life, according to Christian editor Anne Snyder - deseret.com

item.title: Episode 323: The transformative power of gratitude
item.description:
On the Church News podcast, BYU assistant psychology professor Jenae Nelson tells reporter Mary Richards what her new research found when it set thanks directed to God beside gratitude in general and followed each against well-being. The kind she means is not a "naive gratitude" blind to hardship, she says, but trust in God that holds even when life is hard.

  • Episode 323: The transformative power of gratitude - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Church News

item.title: King Charles says Christian faith guides his reign
item.description:
Opening his first General Synod as king on Tuesday, Charles III said his Christian faith is "the compass which guides my every act as sovereign" and paid tribute to his late mother, Queen Elizabeth II, who presided over at least 10 openings of the Church of England's governing body. The king urged members to deepen ties with Catholic and Orthodox Christians, citing recent talks with Pope Leo and Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew, and to keep persecuted Christians in the Middle East and Holy Land in mind. He also asked them to debate in a spirit of unity and to "put yourself in the shoes of those with whom you disagree" when they differ.


Sources:

  • King Charles says Christian faith guides his reign - deseret.com

item.title: Church of Jesus Christ advances 3 temples in Latin America
item.description:
The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints broke ground Saturday, Nov. 14, on temples in Cuernavaca, Mexico, and Piura, Peru, and on Monday the First Presidency released a site map and location for the planned Rivera Uruguay Temple. Presiding in Cuernavaca, Mexico Area President Elder Moisés Villanueva called temples "places of peace" where people can draw closer to God and Christ, while Elder Steven C. Barlow blessed the Piura site, Peru's eighth announced temple. The single-story Mexico and Peru buildings are planned at about 19,000 and 18,800 square feet, and the 9,170-square-foot Rivera temple, near the Brazil border, will eventually be Uruguay's second operating temple.


Sources:

  • Church of Jesus Christ advances 3 temples in Latin America - deseret.com

item.title: How Church-owned camps, new and old, are strengthening youth
item.description:
A short Church News teaser, which sends readers to TheChurchNews.com for the full story, centers on Shipp Family Recreation Camp, a new Church-owned camp for young people described as Georgia's first. The excerpt says a Georgia stake that had staged a pioneer trek for its youth every four years for over two decades was left searching for a new site after a state park canceled its booking about 90 days before the June trek.

item.title: Elder Rasband visits Mia Love’s son on his mission
item.description:
Elder Ronald A. Rasband, an apostle, met with Elder Peyton Love, who is serving a mission in the Dominican Republic, to talk about missionary service and the legacy of Peyton Love's mother, former Utah Rep. Mia Love, who died of glioblastoma in March 2025. The families' ties run through missionary work: Rasband presided over the New York New York North Mission, and Peyton Love said his father, Jason Love, served under Rasband and trained the missionary who baptized Mia Love. Rasband, who recalled Mia Love asking him to bring his favorite Bible to her congressional swearing-in, told Peyton Love that "sometimes the veil is very thin" and that he would feel her presence.

item.title: 10 years on the Conference Center stage: 1 performer’s ‘Luz de las Naciones’ story
item.description:
Amy Ortiz, who first stepped onto the Conference Center stage at 11 in the children's choir of Luz de las Naciones, looks back on performing a 10th year in the Church of Jesus Christ's Spanish-language celebration of Latin American music, dance and faith. Ortiz's family had emigrated from Mexico three years before joining the roughly 1,000-member cast in 2012, hoping the show would keep the children tied to their Mexican heritage, and Ortiz writes that it also bred a love for other cast members' homelands and made it possible to feel at home in both Mexico and the U.S. Recalling moments such as singing This Is the Christ in Spanish that first year, Ortiz credits the performances with strengthening a testimony of Jesus Christ, and Ortiz's mother calls the years of preparation "worth every sacrifice."


Sources:

  • 10 years on the Conference Center stage: 1 performer’s ‘Luz de las Naciones’ story - deseret.com

item.title: Latter-day Saint leader invites followers of Jesus Christ to become peacemakers in ‘hearts, homes and communities’
item.description:
President Dallin H. Oaks' Christmas message, shared Sunday in a YouTube video with his counselors in the First Presidency and included in the December 2026 Liahona, presents Jesus Christ as the Prince of Peace and invites believers to follow his example by making peace in their own lives, families and communities. Oaks described the joy surrounding Christ's birth as a reflection of the "ultimate joy and peace" offered through his Atonement. The article connects the invitation to Oaks' recent focus on peace, including a September National Cathedral address on the Constitution's role in compelling a divided people to work together and Nov. 8 social media posts calling Christ "the way to joy and peace."


Sources:

  • Latter-day Saint leader invites followers of Jesus Christ to become peacemakers in ‘hearts, homes and communities’ - deseret.com

item.title: A sports podcaster toured where young Latter-day Saint men and women prepare to serve missions. Here’s what he learned
item.description:
Drake Toll, host of the Locked on Big 12 podcast, who is not a Latter-day Saint and knew nothing of the Missionary Training Center until BYU athletics invited him, toured the Provo facility last month hours before BYU's 28-24 win over Notre Dame, alongside other media members, athletic director Brian Santiago and former Cougars quarterback Taysom Hill. In a 45-minute meeting, Toll asked missionaries bound for Thailand how they handle misconceptions and hate aimed at their church, and he said their top answer was "to love people, that love unlocks understanding". Weeks later, what stays with Toll is the sacrifice of 18- to 20-year-olds, among them a sister who paused BYU classes to serve and an elder who would know of a BYU win only by spotting fireworks over LaVell Edwards Stadium; being in that room, Toll said, meant getting "to look sacrifice in the eye and hear its voice".


Sources:

  • A sports podcaster toured where young Latter-day Saint men and women prepare to serve missions. Here’s what he learned - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Krysyan Edler

item.title: What Chad Lewis, Morgan Scalley and Kirk Chambers told a teenager about serving missions
item.description:
Provo High School kicker Spencer Shuman, who hopes to play professionally, worried that serving a mission for The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints would cost him his athletic future until a March awards banquet where he talked with former NFL tight end Chad Lewis, Utah coach Morgan Scalley and his own coach, former NFL lineman Kirk Chambers. Each said he would choose his mission again, with Lewis saying he'd pick it over his NFL career and even a Super Bowl. Spencer said the conversations felt like answers to prayers and that a mission might be "something Heavenly Father knew I needed."


Sources:

  • What Chad Lewis, Morgan Scalley and Kirk Chambers told a teenager about serving missions - deseret.com

item.title: Illustrated ‘New Testament Stories’ available online and in print
item.description:
Children can now read a refreshed New Testament Stories, the Latter-day Saint church's illustrated scripture book, which has revised text and new artwork and comes in print as well as a digital edition. Rosemary K. Chibota, who leads the Primary organization, said "a joyful spirit" runs through the book, which Chibota said grew out of a wish to help children connect with scripture and better understand Jesus Christ.

item.title: Why Melissa Dalton-Bradford thinks you should be more political
item.description:
Mariya Manzhos profiles Melissa Dalton-Bradford, a Frankfurt-based Latter-day Saint author who co-founded Mormon Women for Ethical Government and turned her Instagram account, now followed by about half a million people, into a civic-engagement platform after watching Zelenskyy's February 2025 Oval Office clash with Trump. In her new book, How to Save Democracy, she uses histories of collapsed democracies to flag warning signs in the U.S. and urges readers to act, for instance by forming a "democracy defense pod," while maintaining that her work is not partisan and that her deepest identity is as a follower of Jesus Christ. Offering a conservative view, Carolyn Phippen of the Women's Republican Club of Salt Lake City argues both parties should reject departures from the Constitution but faults the left for blaming others, while Dalton-Bradford says the real question is whether today's problems can be addressed "without dismantling democracy".


Sources:

  • Why Melissa Dalton-Bradford thinks you should be more political - deseret.com

item.title: Elder Stevenson participates in World Forum of Intercultural Dialogue
item.description:
Taking part in the 7th World Forum of Intercultural Dialogue in Baku was a highlight of Elder Gary E. Stevenson's Oct. 22-31 assignment in the Europe Central Area, the Church's Europe Newsroom reported. The apostle also met with civic and religious figures in Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan and with Latter-day Saints there and in Paris and Vienna.

item.title: ‘Luz de las Naciones’ celebrates celestial and ancestral roots
item.description:
Around 1,000 volunteers in traditional dress will bring folk music and dance from across Latin America to the Church of Jesus Christ's Conference Center for the 24th annual Luz de las Naciones on Nov. 13 and 14, with Saturday's show streamed live in Spanish and in-person seats sold out apart from a standby line. Elder Jason C. Jensen, the Area Seventy who chairs the show's executive committee, said it is meant for everyone no matter what language they speak, adding, "Jesus Christ is the light of all nations." First-time choreographer Brianna Flores Villaalta replaced the usual Cuban salsa with a caringa courtship dance, saying she wanted "to give more recognition to the Cuban culture".

item.title: Jimmer Fredette tells BYU-Hawaii students to make Jesus Christ their Plan A
item.description:
In a Tuesday devotional at BYU-Hawaii, Jimmer Fredette described how his childhood goal of reaching the NBA came true when the Sacramento Kings drafted him in 2011, then soured into benchwarming, lost confidence and harsh criticism until Elder M. Russell Ballard reached out and challenged him to read the Book of Mormon every day for the rest of the season. Fredette said the reading lifted his mood even though his playing time didn't change, and he came to treat the Savior rather than basketball as his "Plan A", a focus he carried through later pro stints abroad and onto the 3x3 team at the 2024 Paris Olympics.


Sources:

  • Jimmer Fredette tells BYU-Hawaii students to make Jesus Christ their Plan A - deseret.com

item.title: Apostle of the Church of Jesus Christ praises Pope Leo’s ‘sincere desire’ for peace
item.description:
Elder Ulisses Soares, an apostle of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, was in Buenos Aires on a 10-day South America assignment and attended an interfaith gathering Monday at Palacio San Martín, where Pope Leo XIV, partway through his own 12-day trip, told religious leaders that all "religions safeguard human dignity" in his address. Soares said afterward he was impressed by the pope's "sincere desire to invite all people to promote peace in the world." In a social media post, the apostle linked that message to President Dallin H. Oaks' recent appeal for God's children to act as peacemakers by keeping the commandments to love God and neighbor.


Sources:

  • Apostle of the Church of Jesus Christ praises Pope Leo’s ‘sincere desire’ for peace - deseret.com

item.title: Episode 322: Retired Marine Col. Jason Perry speaks about military service, faith and resilience on Veterans Day
item.description:
Jason S.D. Perry, who retired as a Marine Corps colonel after a 30-year military career, now leads wargaming at the Naval Postgraduate School; for Veterans Day, Perry joins Church News reporter Mary Richards on the Church News podcast to reflect on serving as a Latter-day Saint in uniform. The conversation covers faith and resilience, the part chaplains and local Church members and leaders play, and advice for young members considering military service.

  • Episode 322: Retired Marine Col. Jason Perry speaks about military service, faith and resilience on Veterans Day - deseret.com

item.title: Trump, God and forgiveness
item.description:
Asked by Ross Douthat in a 60 Minutes interview whether he could forgive his political enemies if his own entry into heaven depended on it, President Donald Trump answered that he "probably cannot do that, no, because I do hate some of my enemies and I always will". Manzhos notes the exchange came a week after Republicans' midterm losses, as white evangelicals and born-again Christians, who backed Trump at about 82% in each of his three presidential runs, slipped from 23% of 2024 voters to 17% in this midterm, and cites Mark Tooley, president of the Institute on Religion & Democracy, who wrote in The Dispatch that "MAGA Christianity will end" as evangelicals face a post-Trump era. The newsletter also covers Bob Dylan's brief Vatican meeting with Pope Leo and a new documentary on Utah's soda culture.


Sources:

  • Trump, God and forgiveness - deseret.com

item.title: A refreshed youth program reveals Latter-day Saint leaders’ hopes for the next generation
item.description:
Believe, belong and become anchor the three new aims of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints' Children and Youth program, announced Nov. 3 with adjustments that take effect in January 2027. Youth will pick or write their own monthly invitation tied to their For the Strength of Youth lessons and children ages 8 to 11 will set one monthly goal, replacing the current four-area goal structure, while new milestone events and monthly lessons on becoming covenant sons and daughters of God round out the changes. Primary General President Rosemary K. Chibota said the program's purpose has not changed, and Sister Tamara W. Runia of the Young Women general presidency said "Traditions alone will not be enough" to sustain youth once they leave home.


Sources:

  • A refreshed youth program reveals Latter-day Saint leaders’ hopes for the next generation - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Amy Ortiz

item.title: Counterprotesters overwhelm activists targeting Jewish businesses Sunday
item.description:
A bicycle "boycott ride" targeting six Jewish businesses in Philadelphia's Rittenhouse Square on Sunday was outnumbered by hundreds of counterprotesters, who at times formed a wall between the dozens of riders and the restaurants. Police made three arrests, and all six eateries drew long lunchtime lines, with Mac Mart owner Marti Lieberman saying she was "totally overwhelmed" by supporters of every background. Lieberman, who suspects she was singled out because her social media videos show her wearing a Star of David, said she has never mixed religion or politics with her business, while the organizers dismissed any suggestion of a message in the ride's timing, which coincided with the anniversary of Kristallnacht.


Sources:

  • Counterprotesters overwhelm activists targeting Jewish businesses Sunday - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Jacob Hess

item.title: How a Team USA wrestler grappled with the choice to serve a Latter-day Saint mission
item.description:
Team USA wrestler Alex Hedrick stepped away from her sport at 25 to serve a Latter-day Saint mission in New York after placing third at the 2024 Olympic trials, a decision she says became "so clear" to her through prayer. Being six or seven years older than most of her fellow missionaries was a hard adjustment at first, but her mission leaders said her maturity made her a steadying presence, and she kept training on whatever equipment she could find, including wrestling mats at a meetinghouse in her final area. Now back on Team USA with a Grand View Open title and a top-three national ranking, Hedrick is aiming for the 2028 Los Angeles Games and says her mission taught her "I need to be able to be on a team".


Sources:

  • How a Team USA wrestler grappled with the choice to serve a Latter-day Saint mission - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Jason Swensen

item.title: How an artist painted the rotunda of this historic ward house in Cody, Wyoming
item.description:
The dome of Cody, Wyoming's first Latter-day Saint meetinghouse carries a mural of Church history by Edward T. Grigware, a painter who never joined the faith but agreed to the project after local members approached him in the late 1940s. Grigware prepared for close to a year, reading up on the Church's past and traveling to several of its historic sites, before covering the rotunda's 36-foot-diameter ceiling.

  • How an artist painted the rotunda of this historic ward house in Cody, Wyoming - deseret.com

item.title: New ASL Sunday School presidency serves deaf and hard-of-hearing Church members
item.description:
Deaf and hard-of-hearing Latter-day Saints in the United States now have their own ASL Sunday School presidency, which oversees video-based adult religion instruction offered in sign language nationwide. Its president, Marriner Merrill, said the group's aims are those of any Sunday School, from "getting to know our students" to "teaching the gospel in the Savior's way".

  • New ASL Sunday School presidency serves deaf and hard-of-hearing Church members - deseret.com

item.title: Planned Sunday boycott of Jewish-owned businesses in Philadelphia sparks condemnation
item.description:
A Sunday bike rally by the activist group Philly Bike On Your Left, aimed at six Jewish-owned businesses at Philadelphia's Rittenhouse Square under a flyer reading "No business for Zionists" and set for the eve of the Kristallnacht anniversary, has drawn swift condemnation from Pennsylvania officials and national leaders. Gov. Josh Shapiro called the ride "nothing more than blatant antisemitism designed to intimidate" and drive Jewish businesses out, and Mayor Cherelle Parker said singling out owners for being Jewish is unacceptable while affirming the rights of peaceful demonstrators. The group did not respond to media requests but posted a video defending the boycott and denying any deliberate timing, while Hess cites FBI data showing anti-Jewish hate crimes make up roughly 69% of religiously motivated hate crimes.


Sources:

  • Planned Sunday boycott of Jewish-owned businesses in Philadelphia sparks condemnation - deseret.com
item.dc:creator: Jacob Hess

item.title: Learn about the hymn ‘Fight the Good Fight’ in new Latter-day Saint hymnbook
item.description:
The hymn Fight the Good Fight, well known in other churches, now appears with a new tune in Hymns for Home and Church, the global hymnbook of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. Its 1860 text, by the Irish Anglican clergyman and poet John Monsell, takes its theme from Paul's charge to Timothy in 1 Timothy 6:12.

item.title: Apostle’s message inspires Latter-day Saints to shed online anonymity
item.description:
After Elder Quentin L. Cook urged young adults in a worldwide devotional on Sunday, "Please do not hide in anonymity to say unkind or cruel things," many Latter-day Saints had swapped real names onto previously anonymous social media accounts by Monday. Among them was Bryan Summers, who runs the Acts of the Apostles account on X and wrote that "If Elder Cook says it is wise to not be anonymous, I wanna follow him." Cook tied anonymous posting to today's contention and recalled advice from the late Anti-Defamation League leader Abe Foxman, who pointed to the masked Ku Klux Klan as an example of how hidden identity can enable violence.


Sources:

  • Apostle’s message inspires Latter-day Saints to shed online anonymity - deseret.com
